slots.practicalActivity: Install Power BI Desktop from powerbi.microsoft.com or the Microsoft Store, then spend 20 minutes clicking through every ribbon tab (Home, Insert, Modeling, View, Help) and the three view icons (Report/Data/Model) without opening a file yet, just to build a mental map of where things live.
slots.deliverable: A confirmed working install of Power BI Desktop, plus a short written note (3-4 bullet points) describing what each of Get Data, Transform, Model, Visualize, and Publish does.

lessons.title: The Power BI Workflow: Get → Transform → Model → Visualize → Publish

slots.practicalActivity: Download the course's Financial Sample Excel workbook, connect via Get Data > Excel, load the table, drag Profit and a date field onto a column chart, then drag Country onto a map visual sized by Profit.
slots.deliverable: A saved .pbix file ('01-first-report.pbix') containing one column chart and one map built from the Financial Sample workbook.

slots.practicalActivity: Connect to two different source types from the Get Data menu: reopen the Financial Sample as an Excel source, then export one of its sheets to CSV and reconnect to that CSV file, comparing how the Source step differs between the two in Power Query Editor.
slots.deliverable: One .pbix with two separate queries ('FinancialSample_Excel' and 'FinancialSample_CSV') and a written note comparing the Source step generated for each.

lessons.title: Connecting to Web, JSON & REST API Data

slots.practicalActivity: Connect to your SQL Server instance (AdventureWorks2012 or Northwind) via Get Data > SQL Server and import one table; separately connect to a free public JSON API (e.g. jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users) via Get Data > Web. For the SQL connection, check which connectivity modes Power BI offers and decide Import or DirectQuery.
slots.deliverable: A working query against a real SQL Server table and a working query against a REST API, plus a written Import-vs-DirectQuery decision with your reasoning for the SQL source.

slots.practicalActivity: Without lesson guidance, connect to one more data source of a type not yet used this chapter (a different SQL table, a different REST endpoint, or a different file), and write a one-paragraph recommendation of which connectivity mode you'd use for it in production and why.
slots.deliverable: One new, independently built query against an unused source type, plus a written Import/DirectQuery recommendation with reasoning specific to that source.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Financial Sample query in Power Query Editor and walk through every step in the Query Settings pane. Then manually fix the data type of at least 5 columns (e.g. force Date to Date, Units Sold to Whole Number, Gross Sales to Fixed Decimal) and remove rows where Units Sold is blank or zero.
slots.deliverable: A query with your own 'Changed Type' and 'Removed Rows' steps, and a written list of the data type you assigned to each of the 5 columns and why.

slots.practicalActivity: Introduce a deliberate text error (type a letter into a numeric-looking cell in a copy of the source Excel file) and practice Replace Values/Replace Errors to resolve it. Then split the Country column on a delimiter, extract the first 3 characters of Product into a new column, and add a Conditional Column labeling each row 'High Margin' or 'Low Margin' based on a Gross Margin threshold you pick yourself.
slots.deliverable: A cleaned query with explicit 'Replaced Errors', a split/extracted text column, and a conditional column, with your margin threshold and labeling logic noted in writing.

slots.practicalActivity: Pivot the Month Name column into separate columns of summed Sales, then unpivot it back to confirm the round-trip. Use Group By to build a new summary query ('Sales_By_Country') of total Sales and average Profit per Country, then build a small Country-to-Region lookup table and merge it into your main query as a new Region column.
slots.deliverable: A standalone 'Sales_By_Country' summary query produced via Group By, and one merged query with a new 'Region' column pulled from a separate lookup table.

slots.practicalActivity: Split the Financial Sample into two mock year-range tables and Append them back into one stacked table. Create a Power Query Parameter (e.g. a MinUnitsSold threshold) and wire it into a filter step, then review every query you've built so far: rename cryptic step names and set staging queries to 'disable load'.
slots.deliverable: One appended combined-years query, a working parameter that changes filtered results when edited, and a cleaned-up set of queries with renamed steps and non-essential queries set to not load.

slots.practicalActivity: Without following lesson-by-lesson instructions, take a different raw public dataset (e.g. a sample orders export CSV) and independently chain at least 6 Power Query techniques from this chapter — a data type fix, row filtering, a conditional column, a merge with a lookup table, a group-by summary, and a parameter — choosing the order yourself.
slots.deliverable: An original cleaned query, built from a dataset you chose, demonstrating at least 6 distinct Power Query techniques chained together end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Repeat the same 6-technique drill, but this time against a real table in your AdventureWorks2012 or Northwind SQL Server instance instead of a flat file, and note in writing anything that behaves differently against a SQL source — especially what happens to query folding once you add a Conditional Column or a parameter-based filter.
slots.deliverable: A second original cleaned query built against a real SQL Server table, with a written note identifying at least one step that broke query folding.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the Financial Sample data plus the Region lookup table from Chapter 2, classify each table in writing as a fact table or a dimension table, then arrange them in Model view so the fact table sits centered with dimension tables around it, approximating a star schema.
slots.deliverable: A written fact/dimension classification for at least 3 tables and a Model view layout with the fact table centered and dimension tables arranged around it.

slots.practicalActivity: Connect Power BI to your SQL Server instance and import two AdventureWorks2012 tables that don't share an obviously matching column name (Person.Person and Sales.SalesOrderHeader work well). In Model view, draw a relationship between them, explicitly check and set its cardinality, then toggle cross-filter direction from single to both to see the visual change before deciding which direction is correct.
slots.deliverable: A working relationship between two real AdventureWorks2012 tables with cardinality and filter direction set deliberately, plus a one-sentence written justification for your final choice.

lessons.title: Building a Complete Power BI Data Model

slots.practicalActivity: Create a second relationship between two tables already connected elsewhere (forcing it to become inactive), inspect it in Model view, then finish a complete model with at least 3 AdventureWorks2012 dimension tables connected to one fact table.
slots.deliverable: A complete data model in the .pbix Model view with one fact table, at least 3 dimension tables, and one active plus one inactive relationship clearly visible.

slots.practicalActivity: Start a new .pbix, import a fresh set of at least 3 naturally related tables from Northwind (e.g. Orders, Customers, Products), and build a complete star schema from scratch on your own: classify fact vs. dimension tables, create all relationships, and set cardinality and filter direction deliberately for each.
slots.deliverable: A new .pbix ('04-model-review.pbix') with an original, correctly structured star schema model built from real Northwind tables without lesson-by-lesson guidance.

slots.practicalActivity: Connect Power BI to AdventureWorksDW2014's FactInternetSales table and drag SalesAmount onto a card visual to confirm automatic summarization. Then open a new measure and type 3 original DAX expressions from scratch: a literal-number measure, a simple SUM measure, and a measure with an explanatory // comment; finally add one calculated column on the fact table (e.g. a row-by-row profit margin %).
slots.deliverable: 3 original working measures plus one calculated column, all using your own field names and logic rather than copying a lesson's examples, validated in a table visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Create one measure that aggregates something different from your calculated column (e.g. Average Order Value), then write a short explanation in your own words of why a calculated column recalculates per row at refresh while a measure recalculates per filter context at query time. Build 2 new aggregation measures using COUNTROWS and DISTINCTCOUNT on FactInternetSales columns you haven't used yet.
slots.deliverable: One original measure, a short written comparison of columns vs. measures, and 2 new aggregation measures validated in a visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a matrix visual by SalesTerritoryCountry and CalendarYear from AdventureWorksDW2014, then write an original CALCULATE measure of your own design (e.g. 'Sales for one specific country regardless of the row's own country') to directly observe filter context being overridden next to a plain SUM measure. Create a calculated column that references a measure to trigger context transition and note the value you expected versus what you got.
slots.deliverable: A working CALCULATE-based measure shown in a matrix beside a plain SUM measure, plus one demonstrated context-transition example with a written explanation of the result.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 2 original SUMX measures (e.g. a weighted-profit calculation and a custom row-level calculation), then write 2 original measures using CALCULATE filter modifiers (one with KEEPFILTERS, one with REMOVEFILTERS/ALL on a specific column) and one original FILTER()-based measure (e.g. 'Sales for orders above the average order value'), using your own thresholds.
slots.deliverable: 2 original SUMX measures and 3 original filter-modifier/FILTER-based measures, each validated in a card or table visual with sensible, explainable numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: Write an original ALL-based measure (e.g. a '% of Total Sales' using SUM divided by an ALL-wrapped SUM) and an original ALLEXCEPT measure, then build a visual showing an ALLSELECTED measure behaving differently from the ALL measure once a slicer is applied. Pick your 3 messiest measures from this chapter and refactor them using VAR/RETURN.
slots.deliverable: 3 original measures (ALL, ALLEXCEPT, ALLSELECTED) in one visual with a written note on where ALLSELECTED's result differs from ALL's, plus 3 refactored VAR/RETURN measures producing identical results to their originals.

slots.practicalActivity: Drill practice: write 4 original CALCULATE measures, each overriding a different filter (one by country, one by year, one by product category, and one combining two conditions with AND logic inside CALCULATE), and place all 4 side by side in one table visual to compare results.
slots.deliverable: A table visual showing 4 distinct CALCULATE-based measures with visibly different, explainable results, none copied from a lesson's formula.

slots.practicalActivity: Timed drill: in 45 minutes, write 6 new measures combining iterators and FILTER with no lesson reference against AdventureWorksDW2014 — for example 'Average margin for high-value orders only' or 'Total quantity for a specific product category using FILTER instead of CALCULATE's implicit filter'. Check each against a manually calculated expected value in a second table visual.
slots.deliverable: 6 original measures built under time pressure, each cross-checked against an independently calculated expected value.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a 'measure library' table visual listing every measure you've written this chapter (15+) with its result for the current filter context, then clean up the Fields pane by deleting or organizing unused test measures into display folders.
slots.deliverable: An organized measure library visual plus a trimmed Fields pane with unused test measures removed or filed into folders.

slots.practicalActivity: Build your own Date table using CALENDAR or CALENDARAUTO (typed yourself), mark it as a Date table in Model view, add Year/Month Name/Quarter calculated columns, and relate it to FactInternetSales' OrderDate. Then write an original DATEADD measure comparing Sales to the same period last year.
slots.deliverable: A marked Date table joined to the fact table with Year, Month Name, and Quarter calculated columns, plus one original DATEADD-based time-comparison measure.

slots.practicalActivity: Write 3 original time-intelligence measures (YTD Sales, MTD Order Quantity, QTD Profit) using your Date table, then write one original measure using DATESYTD or TOTALYTD with a custom fiscal year-end date, and one using DATESBETWEEN for a specific custom date range relevant to AdventureWorksDW2014's order dates.
slots.deliverable: 5 original time-intelligence measures (YTD/MTD/QTD, one fiscal-YTD, one DATESBETWEEN range) validated against manually counted expected values for a known date range.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a single 'Time Intelligence Dashboard' page combining this chapter's measures: a line chart of YTD Sales vs. prior-year YTD, a card showing QTD Profit, and a year slicer that lets you confirm every measure still recalculates correctly when changed.
slots.deliverable: A working dashboard page where changing the year slicer correctly recalculates every time-intelligence measure without errors.

slots.practicalActivity: For 3 different business questions about AdventureWorksDW2014 (trend over time, comparison across product categories, a single KPI), choose and justify a visual type for each in writing. Build a Table and a Matrix visual showing Sales by SalesTerritoryCountry and CalendarYear with subtotals enabled, then build one bar chart, one line chart, and one pie chart using different field combinations.
slots.deliverable: A written justification for 3 visual-type choices, a Table and Matrix with subtotals enabled, and 3 distinct chart types built from real data.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Card showing a KPI you pick and a Slicer filtering all your charts at once. Apply conditional formatting to a table (a color scale on profit margin, icons on a performance column) using thresholds you set yourself, then configure the Filter pane with one visual-level filter and one page-level filter with different logic.
slots.deliverable: A report page with a card, a working slicer, a table with custom conditional formatting, and at least one visual-level plus one page-level filter.

slots.practicalActivity: Edit visual interactions between two visuals on a page (change one from filter to highlight), then set up a drill-down hierarchy (Year > Quarter > Month) on a chart and a drillthrough page that opens filtered to a selected sales territory.
slots.deliverable: A page with customized visual interactions plus a working drill-down hierarchy and a functioning drillthrough page.

slots.practicalActivity: Add 2 buttons wired to bookmarks that toggle between two different views of the same page (e.g. a 'Summary' vs. 'Detail' state), then add a trend line or forecast to an existing chart using a forecast length you choose yourself.
slots.deliverable: 2 working bookmark-driven buttons that toggle report state, plus a chart with a trend/forecast line configured with a custom forecast length.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original, fully interactive report page combining at least 6 techniques from this chapter without lesson guidance: your own visual choices, conditional formatting, a working filter, customized interactions, a drillthrough, and a bookmark-driven button.
slots.deliverable: A single polished report page demonstrating at least 6 distinct Chapter 7 techniques working together, built from your own design decisions.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page business requirements brief for an invented stakeholder (e.g. 'VP of Sales wants to track regional performance'), listing their top 3 questions, then choose and justify 4 specific KPIs that answer those questions using fields already in your AdventureWorksDW2014 model.
slots.deliverable: A written requirements brief with 3 stakeholder questions and a justified list of 4 KPIs mapped to your data model's fields.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch a dashboard wireframe applying visual hierarchy principles (most important KPI top-left, F-pattern reading order), then write a 3-sentence 'data story' narrative your dashboard should tell a viewer at a glance.
slots.deliverable: A dashboard wireframe sketch with annotated visual hierarchy, plus a written 3-sentence narrative statement for the dashboard.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the executive dashboard your wireframe describes: one page, 4-6 visuals max, a consistent color theme, and your 4 chosen KPIs prominent at the top, following the visual hierarchy you planned.
slots.deliverable: A finished, polished one-page executive dashboard .pbix matching your own wireframe and KPI selections from the previous slot.

slots.practicalActivity: If you have access to a Power BI Service account (a free trial is enough), sign in and compare the Service web UI to Desktop side by side, listing 5 things you can only do in one or the other. Research which license tier your scenario would need, then create a new workspace in Power BI Service.
slots.deliverable: A written 5-item Desktop-vs-Service comparison, a license-tier recommendation with reasoning, and a created workspace in the Service.

slots.practicalActivity: Publish your Chapter 8 executive dashboard .pbix to your workspace using Desktop's Publish button, then locate the semantic model (dataset) behind the published report and review its settings, and share the report under a test scenario configuring its access permissions.
slots.deliverable: Your executive dashboard live in a Power BI Service workspace, with a reviewed semantic model and a configured sharing/permissions setup.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a Power BI App from your workspace, then create a standalone Service dashboard by pinning 3 tiles from your report to it, including at least one tile pinned as a live-updating tile.
slots.deliverable: A Power BI App containing your workspace content, and a Service dashboard with 3 pinned tiles from your report.

slots.practicalActivity: Diagram, in writing, every step a colleague would need to follow to go from your .pbix file on disk to a shared, secured dashboard a VP can open in a browser — publish, workspace, app, sharing permissions — as if onboarding a new team member who has never used the Power BI Service.
slots.deliverable: A written step-by-step onboarding document covering every Service concept from this chapter in the correct order.

slots.practicalActivity: Diagram how refresh works end to end for an Import-mode dataset: source change → gateway → Service → report. If you have a local data source and gateway access, install and register the on-premises data gateway against your SQL Server instance.
slots.deliverable: A written refresh-flow diagram/explanation, plus a registered data gateway if your environment allows it, or documented installation steps if it doesn't.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure a scheduled refresh (e.g. daily) for your published dataset in the Service, then deliberately break the refresh (point it to a renamed/missing table or revoke a credential) and use the Service's refresh history and error message to diagnose it.
slots.deliverable: A configured scheduled refresh setting, plus a written troubleshooting log describing one real or simulated refresh failure and how you diagnosed its cause.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a short incident-response runbook for 'the scheduled refresh failed overnight' — where you'd look first (refresh history), what the 3 most common root causes are based on this chapter, and how you'd confirm the fix worked.
slots.deliverable: A written one-page refresh-failure runbook covering where to look, likely causes, and how to confirm a fix.

slots.practicalActivity: On your AdventureWorksDW2014 star-schema model, create 2 original RLS roles (not copying a lesson example) that each restrict FactInternetSales to a different sales territory or product category using a DAX filter expression you write yourself.
slots.deliverable: 2 working RLS roles defined in Modeling > Manage Roles, each with your own DAX filter condition, tested using 'View As Roles' in Desktop.

slots.practicalActivity: Publish your model with RLS roles to the Service and assign a test role to a user or group (or document the exact steps if you lack admin access), then convert one static role into a dynamic RLS role driven by USERPRINCIPALNAME() against a user-mapping table you build.
slots.deliverable: A dynamic RLS role using USERPRINCIPALNAME() tested with 'View As Roles', plus documented or completed steps for assigning roles to users in the Service.

slots.practicalActivity: Apply your dynamic RLS role to a table 2 relationship-hops away from the user-mapping table (e.g. DimProductCategory via DimProduct), and verify the filter still correctly propagates, adjusting bidirectional filtering or adding a bridge table as needed.
slots.deliverable: A verified RLS test case where the security filter correctly restricts data on a table that isn't directly related to the security table, with a written note on what you had to change in the model.

slots.practicalActivity: Build one original RLS scenario end to end without lesson guidance: design a new role for a real AdventureWorksDW2014 dimension, write its DAX filter, test it with View As, and document how it would behave once published to the Service for a real team you invent.
slots.deliverable: One fully original, tested RLS role with written documentation of its design rationale and expected Service behavior.

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own one-paragraph project brief for the Adventure Works Cycles capstone, using the four requirements from the lesson (regional performance, product-line profitability, reseller fulfillment, year-over-year trend) in your own words, then list which AdventureWorksDW2014 tables each requirement depends on.
slots.deliverable: A written capstone requirements/scope brief naming all four VP-of-Sales requirements and the specific AdventureWorksDW2014 tables each one depends on.

slots.practicalActivity: Import the raw source tables your scope calls for: FactInternetSales, FactResellerSales, DimSalesTerritory, DimProduct, DimProductCategory, DimProductSubcategory, and DimDate from AdventureWorksDW2014.
slots.deliverable: All raw source tables successfully loaded into a new .pbix ('12-capstone.pbix').

slots.practicalActivity: In Power Query, clean and transform every raw capstone table (fix data types, remove errors, handle blanks) so the fact and dimension tables are ready for modeling.
slots.deliverable: A cleaned set of queries in the capstone .pbix, verified in the Power Query Editor with no remaining type or error warnings.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a proper star schema in Model view with FactInternetSales and FactResellerSales as fact tables and the Dim tables as dimensions, setting relationships and cardinality deliberately rather than relying on auto-detection.
slots.deliverable: A complete star-schema data model in the capstone .pbix, verified in Model view with correct cardinality on every relationship.

slots.practicalActivity: Continue building: add a Date table to the capstone model (via CALENDAR/CALENDARAUTO) if DimDate doesn't already cover every need, relate it properly, and double-check every relationship's cardinality and filter direction before moving on to DAX.
slots.deliverable: A capstone model with a working, fully related date dimension and a fully reviewed relationship diagram with no unintended many-to-many or inactive relationships.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the core DAX measures your requirements brief calls for: at least 6 measures covering regional performance, product-line profitability, reseller on-time fulfillment, and year-over-year trend, including at least one CALCULATE-based measure and one time-intelligence measure.
slots.deliverable: At least 6 working, original DAX measures covering all four capstone requirements, validated in a table visual.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the main report page with the primary visuals needed to answer the VP of Sales's top 4 questions: regional performance, product-line profitability, reseller fulfillment, and trend over time.
slots.deliverable: A report page with the primary visuals answering all four stated business questions, using the measures from the previous slot.

slots.practicalActivity: Add interactivity to the capstone report (a drillthrough page to a selected sales territory, a bookmark-driven toggle, or a drill-down hierarchy matching your requirements).
slots.deliverable: A capstone report with at least one interactivity feature functioning correctly against real AdventureWorksDW2014 data.

slots.practicalActivity: Publish the finished capstone report to a Power BI Service workspace (or document the exact publish steps if unavailable), and confirm the published report renders correctly.
slots.deliverable: A capstone report published to the Service, or documented publish steps completed, with the published version confirmed to match Desktop.

slots.practicalActivity: Configure RLS on the capstone model matching the stakeholder scenario (e.g. restrict a regional manager role to their own sales territory) and confirm scheduled refresh still works with security applied.
slots.deliverable: A working RLS role applied to the capstone model with refresh still functioning, tested against at least one restricted role.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliver a 5-minute presentation of the final Adventure Works Cycles dashboard (to a peer, mentor, or recorded for yourself): walk through the business requirement, the data model decisions, the key DAX measures, and the finished dashboard, then note 2 things you'd improve with more time.
slots.deliverable: A completed capstone presentation (live or recorded) covering requirements, model, measures, and final dashboard, plus a written list of 2 concrete 'v2' improvements.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can independently connect to and clean real business data in Power Query, build a proper star-schema data model, write their own DAX measures and time-intelligence calculations, and design, publish, secure, and present a polished, interactive Power BI dashboard end to end.
